Title: Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).
"From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today.
Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule.
He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce the department's workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises.
"In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by the department for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year," he said.
To meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, the department expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide, he said.
He said the fire department currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors.
A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher on positive regional sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, in line with gains across major Asian markets following Wall Street's overnight technology-led rally, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to temper risk appetite.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.60 points to 1,633.35 from Monday's close of 1,631.75.
The benchmark index, which opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, moved between 1,632.77 and 1,641.20 throughout the trading session.
On the broader market, gainers surpassed decliners 667 to 456, while 551 counters were unchanged, 1,108 untraded and 13 suspended.
Turnover decreased to 4.18 billion units worth RM2.95 billion, compared with 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion yesterday.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.349 per cent, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield briefly reached 5.703 per cent.
At the close on Monday, the S&P 500 gained 0.66 per cent to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.05 per cent to 27,477.31.
"On a positive note, Brent crude oil eased below US$100 per barrel as resilient West Asia exports and the Group of Seven's (G7) emergency stockpile release helped alleviate supply concerns," he told Bernama.
Domestically, he said buying interest was seen in telecommunications and commodity-related stocks, while trading activity also broadened to selected small-cap technology, energy and plantation counters.
"We believe selected blue chips could continue to attract bargain hunting following last week's sharp correction.
"However, the lack of follow-through buying over the past three sessions suggests investors remain cautious, with persistent foreign selling and elevated bond yields likely to limit the pace of recovery," he said.
Meanwhile, Thong said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 should provide some support to sentiment.
"The 2027 Budget will be tabled on Friday, with strategic sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, energy transition, pharmaceuticals, logistics, and aerospace among the areas highlighted by the government," he said.
For the rest of the week, he expects the benchmark index to remain in consolidation mode, with a mild recovery bias as oversold conditions provide some downside support.
"Nevertheless, a stronger recovery may require fresh catalysts, with Budget 2027, foreign fund flows, bond yields and geopolitical developments remaining key factors to watch.
"We maintain our FBM KLCI trading range of 1,620-1,650 for the week," he added.
Among the heavyweights, IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 15 sen to RM7.91, while Malayan Banking Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhdeased three sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.70, Public Bank Bhd shed four sen to RM4.67, and Tenaga Nasional Bhd slipped 10 sen to RM12.90.
In active trade, Zetrix AI Bhd and Supermax Corp Bhd improved 2.5 sen to nine sen and 46 sen, respectively, Top Glove Corp Bhd put on nine sen to 87.5 sen, V.S Industry Bhd inched up one sen to 33 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC Bhd slid three sen to 25 sen.
Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd increased RM1.56 to RM44.96, Nestle (M) Bhd rose RM1.26 to RM91.26, Pentamaster Corp Bhd leapt 64 sen to RM6.08, Mi Technovation Bhd jumped 59 sen to RM6.00, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd improved 46 sen to RM21.32.
Top losers were led by Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd, which declined 30 sen to RM29.70, Allianz Malaysia Bhd fell 18 sen to RM20.62, TIME dotCom Bhd trimmed 16 sen to RM5.45, while Mega First Corp Bhd and Ayer Holdings Bhd shaved off 15 sen each to RM2.85 and RM7.55, respectively.

Title: Ringgit ends higher versus greenback ahead of 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed marginally higher against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors kept a close watch on Budget 2027, to be tabled on Friday, for fresh trading cues, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the ringgit climbed to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0845/0890.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027.
He noted that the ringgit maintained its tight range bias today, moving  between RM4.0848 and RM4.0880 while the US Dollar Index (DXY) dipped 0.14 per cent to 102.028 points.  "Still, the DXY remains elevated, with expectations of higher US (interest) rates likely to continue supporting the greenback," he told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major and ASEAN currencies.
The local note gained against the Japanese yen to 2.5807/5837 from 2.5858/5886 at Monday's close, but slid against the euro to 4.5907/5957 from 4.5775/5825 and depreciated against the British pound to 5.4066/4125 from 5.4022/4081 previously.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit appreciated against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 versus 6.52/6.53 at Monday's close, but it edged down against the Singapore dollar to 3.1935/1975 from 3.1905/1943.
The local currency was marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 228.1/228.4 versus 227.9/228.3, and weakened against the Thai baht to 12.1424/1609 from 12.1234/1411. previously.

Title: Countries weigh banning smart glasses over privacy concerns
Article:
Governments, courts and companies are considering restrictions and examining existing rules on smart glasses amid worries that the technology, brought to mainstream by Meta's Ray-Bans, could be used to photograph, film or audio-record confidential materials or people without their knowledge.
Here is a summary of what countries and regions are doing to protect people's privacy, in alphabetical order.
AUSTRALIA
The federal government said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces due to privacy and security concerns.
Public Service Minister Katy Gallagher asked the country's Public Service Commission for advice on whether their use should be prohibited and what exemptions might be required.
BRITAIN
Courts in England and Wales have prohibited the use of Meta smart glasses because of restrictions on taking images and videos in courts.
British cinema operators are also introducing policies to prohibit ​or restrict camera-enabled smart glasses, the UK Cinema Association said in August.
EUROPEAN UNION
Smart glasses have attracted scrutiny from European privacy regulators and some lawmakers, and the European Data Protection Board has commissioned a report into their "social acceptability."
Member of the European Parliament Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová also urged the European Commission, which has not proposed legislation specifically targeting smart glasses, to consider possible action.
NORWAY
The government said it planned to propose a temporary ban on the use of ​AI glasses in places where the public ​regularly gather, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres and public events.
Norway's capital Oslo banned smart glasses in schools in August.
UNITED STATES
New York's Unified Court System banned smart glasses from all its court facilities from July 20. The rule covers prescription and non-prescription eyewear or headwear containing cameras, microphones, computers or other technology capable of recording video or audio. Visitors carrying them must hand them over to court personnel for safekeeping before entering.

Title: Tuaran MP calls for Sabah healthcare upgrade
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's overcrowded hospitals and health clinics need urgent government action, a lawmaker said, calling for concrete and comprehensive measures to address the problem.
Tuaran member of Parliament (MP) Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau said every recommendation in the Health Select Committee's report on its working visit to Sabah should be translated into clear action, funding, timelines and performance measures.
"The issue of overcrowding is not only about the number of patients waiting, but also a shortage of staff, limited treatment space, delays in referrals and weaknesses in patient record management.
"When health clinics lack sufficient space and staff, the pressure is transferred to hospitals. In Tuaran, this pressure eventually reaches referral hospitals in Kota Kinabalu," he said in a statement after debating the report in the Dewan Rakyat here today.
Madius also shared his father's experience at a health clinic in Penampang, where about 200 elderly patients were reportedly waiting for treatment.
He said only two doctors were seen treating patients in a small room, while his father's medical records could not be traced after a blood sample was taken.
He said the matter was referred to the Sabah Health director for investigation, but the records had yet to be found.
Madius said he did not blame doctors or healthcare workers, who were also working with limited space and resources.
"When a patient's records cannot be traced, what is lost is not merely a file. What is disrupted is the patient's medical history, medication, examination results and continuity of care," he said.
He proposed five commitments for the government to consider under Budget 2027, including a special plan to reduce overcrowding at Sabah's hospitals and health clinics, with clear priorities, funding and timelines.
"I also propose the establishment of a Health Services Commission with a specific mandate to plan workforce needs, manage appointments and career pathways, and determine a competitive remuneration framework for healthcare and medical personnel," he said.
He also called for the restoration of regional incentive payments under a progressive structure based on salary, with medical officers given priority as an emergency measure if the scheme could not yet be extended to all civil servants.
Madius proposed a RM5,000 starting bonus for medical officers reporting for permanent placement in Sabah or Sarawak, as well as a RM10,000 retention bonus after completing five years of service.
"Equivalent incentives should be given to Sabah-born doctors serving in Sabah, particularly in rural areas," he said.
Madius said the incentives should be based on the difficulty of the posting and the value of the service, rather than a doctor's state of origin.
He also called for the government to implement an integrated and secure electronic medical records system linking clinics and hospitals to ensure continuity of care and improve the security and confidentiality of patient information.

Title: Myanmar president to begin two-day official visit to Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing will undertake a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning tomorrow.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim would meet the Myanmar leader to discuss several key issues between the two countries.
"These include voluntary, dignified and safe repatriation of Myanmar nationals of all ethnic groups who have been in Malaysia illegally.
"The leaders are also expected to review ongoing efforts undertaken under the Asean mechanisms," it said in a statement on Tuesday.
The Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, said the visit would also provide the Prime Minister with an opportunity to sustain his direct engagement with Myanmar, in line with the decision of the 48th Asean Summit in May 2026 to continue constructive and principled engagement with Myanmar, consistent with the Asean Five-Point Consensus (5PC).
"As Chair of Asean in 2025, the prime minister met with the then Senior General Min Aung Hlaing twice as part of Malaysia's engagement with Myanmar," it said.
In addition, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan visited Myanmar in April and October 2025, as well as in May 2026.
According to Wisma Putra, Myanmar is an integral part of Asean. As a fellow Asean member state, Malaysia will continue to support Asean's efforts to promote peace, reconciliation and access to humanitarian assistance in Myanmar.
"Malaysia will also work closely with all Asean member states to ensure stability and prosperity in the region," it said.

Title: Friend struggles to accept death of student believed strangled by boyfriend
Article:
KUANTAN: A polytechnic student is struggling to accept the sudden death of her close friend, remembering the 19-year-old as a soft-spoken and jovial person who was always there for their regular meals together.
The diploma student, who declined to be named, said they had become batchmates at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Polytechnic last year and shared many simple but memorable moments together.
"We would usually meet up for meals together. The victim was a soft-spoken and jovial person... How could such a thing happen to her?
"There are a lot of memories with her, and I am not sure what life will be like after this," she said before breaking down at the Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital (HTAA) forensic unit today.
It was reported that a female student was found dead, believed to have been
strangled
following an argument with her boyfriend, at a house in Jalan Air Putih.
The suspect has been detained for investigation. Police have yet to disclose the victim's identity.
Meanwhile, a parent who was at HTAA said they rushed there early today after being alerted by their daughter about the incident at the house she was sharing with the victim.
"I am shocked over the whole incident. How can someone commit such an inhumane act? Since the police have arrested the suspect, let them investigate," he said before politely declining further questions.
It is learnt that the victim and three other polytechnic friends, who were all diploma students, were renting two rooms in the three-storey house in Air Putih.
Checks revealed that the 19-year-old suspect was a former polytechnic student who had been expelled due to disciplinary issues.

Title: Fire at Johor Baru shopping complex triggers evacuation
Article:
JOHOR BARU: "My legs were shaking" — that was how one worker described scrambling down the stairs after thick smoke from a burning car filled the basement of Johor Baru City Square shopping and office complex.
Shoppers and workers were evacuated and directed to fire assembly points as firefighters tackled the blaze.
Three people suffered breathing difficulties and received initial treatment from firefighters. A 48-year-old woman was taken to hospital, while two other victims did not require further medical care.
There were no fatalities.
A total of 26 firefighters responded to the incident, led by operation commanders Suffian Sulaiman and Suhaimi Jamal.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 3.40pm.
Firefighters from the Larkin and Tebrau fire and rescue stations arrived six minutes later and found a car on fire at Basement Two, with thick black smoke spreading through the area.
Suffian said operations were still ongoing.
The cause of the fire and extent of damage had yet to be determined.
Posts and videos circulating on social media showed
thick black smoke billowing
from the lower levels of the complex, with some workers describing being forced to evacuate via staircases.
Johor Baru City Square, located just minutes from the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex, is one of the city's best-known shopping destinations and a popular stop for Singaporean visitors.
The mall has more than 200 retailers and 1,250 parking lots, according to its official website.
The complex is also undergoing an upgrading programme as it prepares for the next phase of development around the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link.

Title: Top Glove's margins recover on tighter supply
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The demand-supply balance that occurred from the third quarter (Q3) onwards enabled Top Glove Corp Bhd to recover its margins for the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026 (FY26).
Top Glove joint managing director Lim Jin Feng said there was an increase in average selling prices (ASPs) from Q3 mainly due to the increase in raw material prices, primarily nitrile and latex.
"We were able to pass this cost increase to our customers, mainly because market demand has stabilised.
"We see that the ASP has increased and will depend a lot on the cost of raw material," he said in a press briefing coinciding with the group's full-year performance.
Its corporate director Lim Cheong Guan said the balance between supply and demand in the industry was achieved as lesser capacity was observed during the period under review compared to the period throughout Covid-19, when most of the capacity came from Chinese players.
"There was a sudden, significant increase in our capacity then and right now it is lesser.
"We also saw some constraints on Malaysian manufacturers. Some of us have the spare capacity but there is also a constraint on the workforce.
"So I think that is very important for demand and supply," he said.
Top Glove's earnings more than doubled in FY26 supported by growth in global demand.
Its net profit surged to RM307.96 million from RM105.33 million in FY25 as an improved demand-supply balance allowed manufacturers to rebuild margins after several challenging years.
Revenue for the financial year climbed 21.1 per cent year-on-year to RM4.23 billion from RM3.49 billion last year.
The group said the ongoing Middle East crisis further tightened raw material and glove supply, supporting cost pass-through and contributing to further margin improvement.
"Top Glove's continual quality and cost optimisation initiatives significantly reinforced its global competitive edge.
"The group's strengthened position enabled competitive pricing, driving strong sales volume growth and higher capacity utilisation.
"This was additionally supported by ongoing process automation, which helped mitigate industrywide manpower constraints," Top Glove said in a statement.
Top Glove's net cash position improved to RM141 million in FY26, versus a new debt position of RM267 million in FY25, reflecting a healthier financial structure and increased operational flexibility.
For the quarter ended Aug 31, 2025 (Q4 FY26), its net profit rose more than threefold to RM157.63 million from RM34.83 million. Revenue rose to RM1.25 billion from 893.56 million.
The company announced a tax exempt final dividend of 1.5 sen per share for FY26, payable on Dec 15.
This represents a 213 per cent increase in dividend per share compared with FY25.
The total dividend outlay for FY26 amounts to RM120 million, three times FY25's payout.
Top Glove said the industry outlook remains promising, anchored by steady demand growth for gloves, which remain essential items across the healthcare, industrial and food and beverage sectors.
While challenges including cost increases, raw material supply and price volatility, competition and manpower shortages persist, the group is confident of mitigating these headwinds through continuous quality enhancement and cost optimisation measures.
Top Glove is implementing cost saving measures which include heat energy efficiency partnerships with vendors, as well as expanding artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced automation across operations.
This safeguards margins and maintains cost leadership to manage upcoming cost pressures, particularly the scheduled increase in natural gas tariffs effective Oct 1.
"The continued demand for gloves provides a solid foundation for long-term growth," said executive chairman Tan Sri Lim Wee Chai.
"While market conditions remain dynamic, the group's strong focus on working hard, smart and fast, coupled with improvements in quality and cost efficiency, people productivity and AI integration, will ensure we remain competitive and well-equipped to navigate industry challenges," he added.

Title: Trump urges supporters to vote by mail despite fraud claims
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump encouraged supporters on Saturday and again on Monday to vote by mail if they wanted, a change of tone for the US president, who has for years described mail-in voting as a practice rife with fraud.
Speaking to reporters at the White House before departing for a rally in Nebraska on Monday afternoon, Trump said his supporters could vote by mail in the coming congressional midterm elections on Nov 3, even as he said he preferred in-person voting.
"They can vote by mail if they want, because we seem to have no choice because a lot of people want to vote by mail, but a lot of very good people also want to vote in-person," Trump said. "You can do either."
The comments came after he posted a campaign video over the weekend encouraging Republicans to vote.
"Vote early, vote by mail or vote in-person on Election Day, November 3rd," Trump said.
It was not immediately clear why Trump changed his tone. The president has repeatedly made false claims that his 2020 election defeat was the result of voter fraud, including with mail-in ballots.
The Trump administration tried to significantly tighten the rules governing mail-in voting heading into the midterm elections, though the Supreme Court in September declined to allow the Postal Service to enforce the new rules.
Some Republicans have in the past expressed concern that discouraging mail-in voting could reduce turnout among conservative rural voters, a core part of Trump's base, some of whom live relatively far from polling stations.
Republicans are entering the final weeks of the campaign in a difficult national political environment.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday found Trump's approval rating at 32 per cent, holding at September's record low, while registered voters preferred Democrats over Republicans 44 per cent to 37 per cent when asked which party they would support in the midterms.
Among independents, Democrats led 37 to 21 per cent, with 28 per cent undecided.

Title: Six Perak petrol stations inspected over alleged RON95 contamination
Article:
IPOH: Six petrol stations in Ipoh, Taiping and Kuala Kangsar have been inspected following complaints that RON95 petrol was allegedly contaminated with water and had damaged consumers' vehicles.
Perak Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Datuk Kamalludin Ismail said the inspections were carried out following public complaints and viral social media posts concerning the alleged contamination.
"Preliminary checks using manual dipping methods and the Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) system found no indication of water contamination in the fuel storage tanks inspected," he said in a statement.
However, he added that the preliminary findings could not be regarded as conclusive.
"Fuel samples had been taken from the storage tanks and pumps involved and submitted to the Department of Chemistry for detailed scientific analysis.
"The ministry has not made any conclusions regarding the allegations until the official analysis results are obtained and the investigation is completed," he said.
He said the inspection also involved physical checks of the fuel storage systems, including manual dipping using dipsticks or dip rods, with the readings cross-checked against the ATG system.
"Officers also collected and reviewed records of fuel deliveries, sales transactions and other relevant documents from the petrol station operators for the period concerned," he said.
He said the ministry would examine the laboratory analysis results together with the overall findings of the investigation before deciding on further action.
"Should any violation of the laws enforced by the ministry be established, firm action without compromise will be taken against those responsible," he said.
He also advised the public against drawing premature conclusions based on information circulating on social media.
Consumers can lodge complaints with the ministry through WhatsApp at 019-848 8000, the e-aduan portal, its 1-800-886-800 call centre or the Ez ADU KPDN smartphone application.

Title: Activists demand amnesty for protesters as Thailand marks 1976 massacre
Article:
BANGKOK: Activists called for amnesty for people prosecuted under Thailand's strict royal insult law on Tuesday, during a ceremony marking 50 years since a massacre of demonstrators protesting dictatorship.
A small group shouted "Amnesty 112" from a balcony at Bangkok's Thammasat University, an AFP reporter saw, as around 300 people including politicians and survivors gathered to commemorate the Oct 6, 1976, killings on the campus.
Under Section 112 of Thailand's criminal code – which was tightened after the 1976 massacre – anyone convicted of insulting, defaming or threatening the king or his family can face a prison sentence of up to 15 years per offence.
Legal observers and rights campaigners say the law is interpreted so broadly that it has become a tool to target dissent.
Nearly 300 people have been charged under the so-called lese majeste law since 2020, including many young people who took part in large-scale protests that year to demand democratic change and reform of the monarchy.
The Thammasat crackdown 50 years ago followed the return from exile of military dictator Thanom Kittikachorn, who had been ousted three years earlier.
Students had gathered to oppose his return. Police and right-wing groups stormed the campus, shooting, beating and lynching protesters.
The official death toll was 46, although survivors and witnesses believe more than 100 were killed. No state official has been held accountable.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was represented at Tuesday's ceremony at the university memorial by a junior minister.
"Today we pay tribute and express our condolences for the lives lost," Minister Paradorn Prissananantakul told AFP after laying a wreath.
Asked why the government never held its own service for the victims, he did not answer directly, saying that "the most important lesson from the October incident, on the government side, is to open the floor to everyone who has different opinions, so they can express their voices."
Thammasat survivor Wattana Chaichanasakul had earlier read out the names of those killed, a tradition observed every year.
It is to "remind ourselves that we will never forget our friends because if we do, it means we kill them again", she told the audience.
Current student Thanaporn Singlee, 21, said it was important to mark the anniversary because "Thammasat was a place where people died because of the government."

Title: Why polls keep getting it wrong on Brazil's right
Article:
ONCE again, Brazilian pollsters missed the mark in a first-round election on Sunday, joining many around the world who have struggled to guage support for the right from voters who can be cagey about their choices.
"I am very pleased because many polling institutes had us trailing," right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro said after edging past President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's election.
He is now a firm favourite as the race goes to a runoff vote on Oct 25.
The son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, the opposition candidate secured nearly 47 per cent of the vote, compared to Lula's 45 per cent.
The Datafolha pollster had Lula three percentage points ahead of his rival in the first round, while Quaest showed a one point lead for Lula.
Survey firms have been blindsided in other countries too.
In the United States, some polls wrongly predicted a victory for Democrat Kamala Harris over Donald Trump in 2024 elections.
In Latin America, polls also failed to anticipate the strong showing of libertarian firebrand Javier Milei in Argentina or conservative Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia.
Right-wing and far-right forces in Europe have also bucked predictions.
In many cases, these parties have positioned themselves as anti-establishment options and capitalise on social discontent.
"There is the phenomenon of the 'shy vote' phenomenon, where voters don't choose a candidate on their merits, but because they dislike the other options," Marco Carvalho Teixeira, a political scientist at the Getulio Vargas Foundation, told AFP.
Such voters will not disclose their choice to pollsters.
Brazil's first-round election also featured "high volatility" among undecided voters right up to the end of the campaign, making predictions difficult, says Carvalho Teixeira.
James Bosworth, a consultant and author of the Latin American Risk Report, a political risk newsletter, said pollsters overestimated the support of third-party candidates who garnered only eight per cent of the vote on Sunday.
He said some voters who had expressed support for one of the smaller candidates "voted strategically" and opted for one of the leading candidates in a bid to make their vote count – which Bolsonaro had pushed hard for on the campaign trail.
Nevertheless, the polling error was smaller this year than in the first round of elections in 2022 when polls gave Lula a 10 point advantage over Jair Bolsonaro. He came first by only five.
"In the last four elections, the Brazilian right performed three to four per cent better than the polls predicted," Bolsonaro's campaign manager, senator Rogerio Marinho, told AFP ahead of the vote.

Title: Pay households, businesses to store power: Industry players
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Households and small businesses should be paid to store electricity and help ease pressure on Malaysia's power grid, industry players said.
Suncrox Solar founder Noor Shahiwan said consumers who store excess electricity and reduce their reliance on the grid during peak periods should be compensated for the wider benefit they provide to the power system.
Speaking at the 5th Solar Energy Storage Future Malaysia 2026, he said such incentives could encourage more consumers to install behind-the-meter energy storage.
He said the government could target users based on their ability to reduce grid demand, rather than offering blanket incentives, as different consumers have different electricity-use patterns.
For example, small shops and offices that operate mainly during daylight hours could use batteries to meet their electricity needs after solar generation falls in the late afternoon.
Similarly, households could use stored solar power during the evening peak, reducing their need to draw electricity from the grid when demand rises.
Shahiwan said such consumers should be incentivised because they not only manage their own electricity costs but also help the wider power system.
"The impact is very high and much bigger than, let's say, if you have a commercial industry," he said in a panel discussion titled "Malaysia Energy Transition 2026: What's Next After Solar ATAP?".
He said the government could classify consumers according to their level of dependence on the grid and structure incentives accordingly.
This could include grid-dependent, less grid-dependent and non-grid-dependent users, with greater incentives for consumers that can provide more flexibility through energy storage.
The proposal comes as Malaysia's electricity demand profile changes rapidly, driven by data centres, electric vehicles and broader electrification.
Solar generation, however, is concentrated during daylight hours, creating a need for storage and other forms of flexibility as renewable energy penetration increases.
Shahiwan said behind-the-meter storage could also help households on time-of-use tariffs avoid drawing electricity from the grid during periods of higher demand.
He said energy storage should therefore be considered alongside rooftop solar rather than as a standalone technology.
He said energy storage and energy efficiency should be the next priorities after rooftop solar as Malaysia needs to address both how electricity is generated and how efficiently it is consumed.
Shahiwan said financial incentives would be important if the government wanted to accelerate the deployment of behind-the-meter storage.
Rather than simply subsidising equipment, he said the policy should recognise the value that consumers could provide by reducing peak demand and improving the overall flexibility of the electricity system.
Solaroo Systems Sdn Bhd co-founder and director Johann Sze said battery storage was already becoming an urgent requirement.
"There is a lot more energy that is needed at night, which is straining our grid," he said.
He said the large-scale solar programme LSS6 had also moved towards incorporating battery storage, reflecting the growing need to balance renewable energy generation.
The LSS6 covers 2,500MW of solar capacity paired with 1,250MW of battery storage, with projects targeted for operation by 2029.
Meanwhile, SOLS Energy deputy chief executive officer Jaran Walia said Malaysia also needed to accelerate grid investment and streamline the approval process for rooftop solar.
"I don't know if we are investing fast enough upfront for our future grid requirements," he said.
He said there was a lot of opportunity for optimisation in the paperwork and end-to-end process for solar adoption, which could make turnaround times faster for consumers.

Title: Villa used as scam centre targeting Japanese
Article:
MELAKA: A villa in a village area, rented for tens of thousands of ringgit a month, was found to have been used as an operations centre for a telephone scam syndicate targeting victims in Japan.
The operation was uncovered after police raided the villa at Jalan Lama Bukit Punggor, Kampung Bukit Punggor, Alai, here, at 2.30pm on Sunday.
Melaka Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the raid was conducted by the district police headquarters' Commercial Crime Investigation Division (CCID) following intelligence and surveillance.
He said 17 foreign nationals, comprising 11 Japanese, four Chinese and two Myanmar nationals aged between 23 and 55, were arrested.
"Those detained comprised 14 men and three women.
"Checks found several individuals in front of computer equipment placed in three separate rooms among the nine rooms at the premises," he said at a press conference at the Melaka Tengah district police headquarters here today.
Halim said police also seized 21 mobile phones of various brands, a laptop, two monitors, two central processing units (CPUs), two keyboards, two mice, a router, a notebook, 28 sheets of computer printouts believed to contain scripts in Japanese and two gate remote controls.
The total value of the seized items was estimated at RM25,000.
He said the villa was believed to have been used as an operations centre for a telephone scam targeting Japanese.
"The syndicate is believed to have started operating in Melaka in early August, with all the suspects believed to have been involved in identifying and contacting Japanese victims by telephone.
"Police also found 28 sheets of computer printouts believed to contain scripts in Japanese, which are being examined as part of the investigation," he said.
Halim said the methods used to deceive victims, call scripts, identities used, payment methods, flow of funds and total losses were still under investigation.
"Further analysis of the seized items is also being conducted to establish the full modus operandi, the roles of each suspect, the identity of the syndicate mastermind, the victims involved and the group's financial flows.
"This is the first time police have arrested syndicate members involving Japanese," he said.
Halim said the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code, with all 17 suspects remanded for 14 days from yesterday until Oct 18.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dana Impak mobilises RM2.6bil for 130 firms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah Nasional Bhd's Dana Impak has mobilised RM2.6 billion in investments to support around 130 Malaysian and Malaysian-linked companies and more than 4,200 talent, according to the Dana Impak report.
The report, launched on Tuesday, also sets out Dana Impak's catalytic role in crowding in capital and strategic partners alongside Khazanah.
This reflects a broader whole-of-Malaysia approach to support the growth of Malaysian companies and entrepreneurs.
As at Dec 31, 2025, RM905 million deployed into these companies had directly crowded-in RM433 million of external capital, equivalent to 48 sen for every RM1 invested by Khazanah.
Managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir said as a purpose-driven, long-term investor, Khazanah recognised that Malaysia's resilience increasingly depends on the strength of its own firms, particularly as capital becomes more selective and global markets more complex.
"The progress of Dana Impak reflects a collective effort, with the government, investors, fund managers, industry partners and institutions coming together to strengthen Malaysia's firms across their growth cycles, improve their investability and enable access to deeper pools of capital over time.
"Looking ahead, Dana Impak will continue to deepen capabilities and talent in strategic ecosystems.
"Under the Ministry of Finance's GEAR-uP initiative, we will continue to mobilise capital and partnerships to support more Malaysian companies and entrepreneurs scale, compete globally and capture a greater share of the value they create," he added.
Since 2024, Dana Impak has sharpened its focus towards a programmatic approach across three focus areas: venture capital and startup ecosystem, mid-tier companies and semiconductor and advanced manufacturing.
Through Jelawang Capital, Dana Impak is strengthening Malaysia's venture and startup ecosystem with an allocation of up to RM1 billion, expanding access to early-stage funding while building a stronger pool of local and established regional fund managers.
Jelawang Capital has supported five Malaysian fund managers under its Emerging Fund Managers' Programme and committed two fund managers under the Regional Fund Managers' Initiative.
For mid-tier companies, capacity development is paired with private equity, private credit solutions and direct investments to strengthen capabilities and expand access to growth capital.
In semiconductor and advanced manufacturing, specialist fund managers and strategic investments are helping build higher-value technology, industrial and talent capabilities in Malaysia.
This includes Khazanah's support for SkyeChip, from its early-stage journey through to a leading cornerstone investment in its initial public offering.
Cambrian Fund, a partnership between Khazanah, the co-founders of ViTrox and Southern Capital Group, raised RM104.5 million to support Malaysia's next generation of IR4.0 entrepreneurs.

Title: Unhealthy air readings rise to 30 areas, Batu Pahat tops
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of areas with unhealthy air quality rose to 30 as of 5pm today, up from 20 at 7am, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
The highest reading was at Batu Pahat, Johor, at 196, just below the very unhealthy threshold of 201. It was followed by Nilai, Negri Sembilan, at 174.
Four stations tied at 171: Seremban in Negri Sembilan, Segamat, Pasir Gudang and Tangkak in Johor.
Johor had the most stations with unhealthy readings, at eight. Besides those above, they were Kluang (168), Larkin (166), Kota Tinggi (162) and Pengerang (160).
Selangor and Pahang each had five stations in the unhealthy range. In Selangor, the readings were Johan Setia and Shah Alam (163 and 161), Petaling Jaya and Banting (157 each) and Klang (153).
In Pahang, Indera Mahkota in Kuantan recorded 160, followed by Jerantut (159), Balok Baru in Kuantan (157), Rompin (152) and Temerloh (143).
Melaka had three stations in the unhealthy range: Melaka city (164), Bukit Rambai (158) and Alor Gajah (157). Besides Nilai and Seremban, Negri Sembilan's Port Dickson recorded 155.
In the Klang Valley, Putrajaya recorded 166, while Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 163 and 158 respectively.
Terengganu's Kemaman and Paka each recorded 156, while Tanjung Malim in Perak, at 116, had the lowest reading among the unhealthy stations.
Another 33 areas recorded moderate readings, while five were in the good range. None recorded a very unhealthy reading.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous.

Title: RTS Link tackles gradient, wet-weather braking challenges
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A three per cent viaduct gradient and wet-weather braking are among the engineering challenges being tackled to ensure safe and reliable operations on the RTS Link.
RTS Operations (RTSO) chief executive officer Dr Ahmad Marzuki Ariffin said the cross-border rail link might appear straightforward with only two stations, but its trains, tracks, signalling systems and infrastructure must work seamlessly to deliver a safe journey.
He said the viaduct's three per cent gradient, which is the maximum slope allowed for train operations on the RTS Link, required close coordination between track design, braking and signalling systems.
"Two countries. Two stations. One sea crossing. There are many complex engineering challenges.
"The RTS Link may seem relatively straightforward, as it only has two stations.
"But a safe and reliable journey depends on careful engineering.
"The trains, tracks, signalling systems and infrastructure must work together seamlessly.
"One such challenge is to address the viaduct's three per cent gradient. This is by design, the maximum slope allowed in the RTS Link for train operations," he said in a statement today.
Trains descend along this slope from the bridge's highest point towards ground level. They must maintain a safe speed and stop smoothly and accurately at the station.
This requires careful coordination of the track design, braking and signalling systems, he said.
"Wet weather adds another challenge. Rain can reduce grip between the wheels and rails. This affects how trains accelerate and brake. Thorough testing is therefore essential to ensure safe and reliable operations in different weather conditions.
"This is just one example of the engineering solutioning that must be accomplished for every safe and comfortable journey. It involves many hours of design thinking, testing and teamwork," he added.
The RTS Link, originally targeted to begin operations on Jan 1, 2027, has now been pushed back to February 2027, with the revised launch subject to final safety certification and approvals.
Infrastructure works on the 4km link between Bukit Chagar station in Johor Baru and Woodlands North station in Singapore are substantially complete.

Title: 'It's okay, bro': Marshal took longer route to help George Russell cool down
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A race marshal who gave Formula One driver
George Russell a lift back to the pits on his motorcycle
took a longer route after seeing how disappointed the Mercedes driver was following his late retirement in Sunday's race.
The marshal, identified only as Awang, said Russell was barely able to speak after he picked him up beside his stranded car.
Speaking in a radio interview, Awang said he offered words of encouragement to Russell, who had been running third when his race ended five laps from the finish at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia..
"I just told him, 'It's okay, bro. You can do it better.'
"He lowered his head. Then, as he sat behind me, he leaned his head against my shoulder," he said.
Awang said Russell's reaction prompted him to take a slightly longer route before returning him to the pits.
"I thought perhaps I should take him on a slightly longer ride, to let him calm down and cool off, before reaching the pits," he added.
Russell had been
running third behind
eventual winner Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli when a power unit failure ended his race during a safety car period on Sunday.
He stopped on the main straight before climbing off his car and shaking his head, as what had looked set to be a podium finish slipped away.
The retirement was another setback for Russell, who had expressed frustration over repeated problems this season. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff later confirmed the power unit failure.
Russell's retirement also saw his deficit to championship leader Antonelli widen from 66 to 84 points, leaving the Briton conceding that his title hopes were now exceptionally slim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mahfuz: Pas must resolve PN turmoil before seeking to lead Melaka
Article:
MERLIMAU: Pas must prove it can provide clear leadership and unity within Perikatan Nasional (PN), said Amanah vice-president Datuk Mahfuz Omar.
He said the party should first resolve the coalition's internal uncertainty before seeking to convince voters it was ready to lead a state or the country.
"The coalition's current turmoil over its suspended activities, registration status and election symbol raised questions about Pas' ability to lead a complex political alliance, particularly ahead of the Melaka state election.
"More interestingly, Pas itself is now facing questions over the use of its logo, the position of component parties and the coalition's direction.
"When Pas took over PN's leadership from Bersatu, the question is whether PN became stronger or more fragmented," he said in a statement today.
His remarks came a day after PN filed a
judicial review application
to challenge the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) suspension of its activities and a notice that could lead to the coalition's deregistration.
PN's electoral position has also remained uncertain, with its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan previously saying the coalition could use Pas' logo or that of another component party if the suspension remained in force.
Bersatu, meanwhile, has indicated it may contest under its own logo if the PN issue remains unresolved.
Mahfuz said he was not blaming Pas for all of PN's problems but argued that the party should be judged by the outcome of its leadership.
"Today, even the flag is unclear, the logo is still being questioned and the direction remains unconvincing," he said.
He said PN leaders should not blame the government for disputes within the coalition, saying internal problems should be resolved internally.
"RoS did not create PN's internal problems. If there are disputes among component parties, they should be resolved by PN's leadership," he said.
Mahfuz also referred to Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang's recent statement that the party was prepared to use either its own logo or the Barisan Nasional logo in the
Melaka election
, depending on ongoing negotiations.
He said Melaka voters were ultimately interested in knowing not only which logo would appear on the ballot paper, but who was steering the political coalition and where it was headed.
"If Pas truly wants to lead PN, this is the time to prove that it can unite, not create confusion; determine a direction, not add uncertainty; and build confidence, not merely slogans.
"Don't ask the people to hand over the state's helm to those who are still arguing over which flag their ship should fly," Mahfuz said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MediAsas basic medical insurance scheme to expand next year
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The government will expand the basic medical insurance scheme next year as part of reforms to tackle rising premiums and healthcare inflation, says Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin.
Sim, who has been championing the issue of rising medical insurance premiums and private healthcare costs, said the MediAsas scheme is currently being piloted and is expected to be rolled out in the first quarter of next year.
Sim, who is also the Bayan Baru member of parliament, said he raised concerns over escalating medical insurance premiums and private hospital charges in parliament in 2024, prompting government action.
"What is important is that the government has announced a basic medical insurance for Malaysians who can afford medical insurance but are now feeling burdened by the rising premiums," he said.
He said MediAsas was among 12 initiatives under the government's reform of private healthcare financing, with measures aimed at addressing the underlying factors driving up insurance costs.
Expanding the insurance pool is crucial to making medical coverage more sustainable and affordable, he added.
"This is about increasing the pool. If the pool is bigger, we can control pricing. If the pool is small, each insurance company creates its own small pool," he said.
Sim said the scheme would cater to Malaysians who could afford insurance, while those unable to pay for coverage could continue relying on public healthcare.
"Not everyone can afford insurance. Those who cannot afford it can go to the government, while those who can afford it can join this pool," he said.
Sim said government action gathered momentum following his parliamentary interventions, leading the Public Accounts Committee to conduct an investigation and issue a comprehensive report in 2025.
He said a joint reform effort involving the Health Ministry, Bank Negara Malaysia and the Finance Ministry had also been established to address private healthcare financing and insurance.
Sim said the reforms would take time to implement because of the complexity of the healthcare system, but expressed confidence they would help contain medical inflation and ease pressure on insurance premiums.
"I'm pretty optimistic that this will be able to control medical inflation that is too high," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tunku Ismail meets MACC chief, newly appointed Johor director
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tunku Ismail, Regent of Johor, granted an audience to Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman at Istana Pasir Pelangi yesterday.
Newly appointed Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid was also present during the audience, according to a post on the official HRH Crown Prince of Johor Facebook page.
The meeting served as Hazrul Shazreen's official courtesy call following his appointment, which took effect on Oct 1.
During the audience, the MACC leadership reaffirmed the agency's commitment to strengthening anti-corruption enforcement and prevention efforts, as well as enhancing integrity and governance in Johor.
"The meeting reflects the continuing working relationship between the MACC and the Johor Royal Institution in supporting the agenda of integrity and good governance," the post said.

Title: Monsoon transition phase to bring heavy rain, thunderstorms from Oct 9
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The monsoon transition phase is expected to begin on Oct 9 and continue until late October, marking the end of the Southwest Monsoon which began on May 14.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said in a statement today that the country will experience weak winds blowing from various directions during this phase, creating conditions conducive to the formation of thunderstorm clouds.
"This situation typically brings heavy rain and lightning accompanied by strong winds over a short period, particularly during the afternoon and early evening in most areas in the west and interior of the Peninsula, as well as western Sabah and Sarawak," he said.
"These weather phenomena have the potential to cause flash floods, water surges, fallen trees, and damage to unstable structures."
He added that with the end of the Southwest Monsoon, transboundary haze from neighbouring countries is expected to diminish gradually following changes in wind patterns.
The public is advised to exercise greater caution during this period and stay updated on weather forecasts and warnings issued by METMalaysia through its official website, myCuaca mobile application, and official social media platforms.
Enquiries can also be directed to the department's hotline at 1-300-22-1638, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-German spy chief arrested for espionage, treason: Prosecutors
Article:
BERLIN: Germany's former foreign spy chief was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of espionage, accused of seeking to pass sensitive information to overseas intelligence services, prosecutors said.
August Hanning, who ran Germany's BND intelligence agency between 1998 and 2005, is suspected of charges including "attempted treason" and "espionage", according to a statement from federal prosecutors.
Hanning's former chief of staff, partially named as Manfred D., was also arrested on suspicion of "aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage."
Premises linked to both men are being searched in several locations including the capital Berlin.
Prosecutors say that Manfred D. also served as the chief of staff for Hanning's successors between 2012 and 2026, and used this role to gain access to confidential information which he then passed on to Hanning "in exchange for remuneration."
"The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D. provided Hanning with approximately two thousand documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the Federal Intelligence Service for internal purposes," prosecutors say.
They allege that "on one occasion, Hanning used classified intelligence ... to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service", although it is not clear if "the material reached the intended recipient."
Hanning is also accused of being "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D., for several years."

Title: Health Ministry mulls study on family breakdowns linked to doctors' postings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is considering a baseline study to determine whether long-distance postings are contributing to family breakdowns among medical officers.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry currently lacked specific data on divorces or other family problems linked to medical officers being posted far from their spouses and children.
"I believe there is a need for us to conduct a baseline study on the extent to which their families are affected by prolonged separation due to their positions, duties, and careers," he said in the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to V. Ganabatirau (PH-Klang), who raised concerns over bullying, postings, transfers, welfare, and the brain drain among ministry medical officers.
Dzulkefly said posting decisions are based on departmental needs and vacancies, while taking into account qualifications, competency, experience, length of service, distance from the workplace, dependants, and health conditions of officers or their family members.
He said about 74 per cent of posting applications have been successfully accommodated, while the rest could not be fulfilled due to factors including a lack of vacancies.
On transfers, Dzulkefly said there is no standard waiting period as decisions depend on application dates, cycle deadlines, committee meetings, and service requirements, with transfer exercises conducted at least four times a year.
He said the ministry also provides a mutual transfer system (P3S), which has matched 118 pairs of nurses, alongside eight cases involving service requirements and 18 in the pharmacy service.
On workplace bullying and toxic culture, Dzulkefly said the ministry launched the Guidelines for Managing Workplace Bullying for ministry personnel on Aug 21, 2025, covering reporting, prevention, and intervention procedures.
He said 730 complaints were recorded through the system from Oct 1, 2022 to Sept 28 this year, with four found to be substantiated and acted upon, while the remaining 726 involved various issues including services, operations, transfers, and communication.
Dzulkefly assured that whistleblowers will be protected from any action by their superiors.
"As the minister, I will not compromise on this matter... I want them to be protected," he said.

Title: Thousands mass in France for high school protests
Article:
PARIS: Thousands of demonstrators were massing under heavy police surveillance Tuesday in Paris and cities across France, as unions and teachers joined high school students who for days have been demanding better conditions in protests punctuated by violent clashes.
Students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds since late September, complaining of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures.
In the Paris suburb of Creteil, where the protests started last month, students have piled barriers outside the Saint-Exupery high school.
"We are here to make our voice heard, all too often forgotten," student Abderrahmane Abdelkader said on the microphone.
In the western city of Rennes, teacher Romain Dubourgn said he and other teachers were present to show support.
"With about thirty colleagues, we talked about the police brutality we've witnessed and decided to be there for our students if they need us," he told AFP.
While many protests have been peaceful, some demonstrators have lit dustbin fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police, who have responded with batons, tear gas and riot-control rounds.
The government says 215 students and 715 police officers have been injured since the start of the movement, with a 15-year-old losing a hand on Monday after, according to a police union source, he picked up a sting-ball grenade fired by riot officers.
Television images Tuesday showed anti-riot police with shields pushing back crowds who had formed a human chain and blocked a road by a school in eastern Paris.
There were protests taking place in Marseille in the south, Nantes in the west and Lyon in the southeast, AFP correspondents said.
The unrest has erupted with just months to go before the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron after his maximum two terms in office.
The government has sought to address the grievances, while accusing the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of being behind the movement.
Veteran LFI presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has strongly supported the protests, while calling for non-violent methods.
Authorities are expecting some 20,000 to 40,000 demonstrators in Paris.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office has called for "peaceful" gatherings, calling for a return to "a structured, legal and democratic form of opposition."
[[nid:1549097]]
The head of the CGT labour union Sophie Binet has said its members would be there to "protect high-school students."
Greens party leader Marine Tondelier has urged local officials and parents to wear white and "go and protect our children during demonstrations."
Several unions and rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force against the protesters.
Amnesty International late Monday said the French authorities should "put an end to the disproportionate police repression seen in recent days during student protests."
"The images and testimonies widely circulated over the past week raise alarming concerns about the dangerous use of tear gas, batons and policing techniques by the police," Amnesty's Anne Savinel-Barras said.
The police have launched 10 internal investigations into allegations of brutality since the protests started, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said late Monday.
Since the start of the movement, 24 schools have been burned or ransacked, according to the education ministry.
More than 5,000 people, 87 per cent of them minors, have been arrested.
Lecornu's office said 85 teaching staff have also been injured.
The prime minister has sought to address the issue of missing teachers and renovating buildings that are dilapidated.
The government is also pushing legislation to make those responsible for damaging public property pay for repairs themselves, instead of using public funds.

Title: High Court postpones Altantuya judicial review hearing to Jan 12
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today postponed to Jan 12, 2027, the hearing of a judicial review application by the father of the late Altantuya Shaariibuu.
The application seeks to compel police to investigate supplementary affidavits and a statutory declaration by former police officer Chief Inspector Azilah Hadri.
Lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo, representing Altantuya's father, Dr Shaariibuu Setev, said the adjournment followed the respondents' request to file an affidavit in reply to one submitted by her client today.
In the application, Shaariibuu named the Inspector-General of Police, the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director, the police , the Attorney-General, and the Malaysian government as respondents.
Sangeet said in written submissions, the respondents contended that the applicant had not provided information under Section 107 of the Criminal Procedure Code, and thus they were under no obligation to inform him of the investigation status.
"In response, we submitted to the court a police report lodged by the applicant in 2018, which specifically requested an investigation to identify the party who ordered the murder of Altantuya Shaariibuu," she said when met today.
"The respondents requested an opportunity to respond to the contents of that affidavit. Therefore, the court adjourned the hearing to Jan 12, 2027, to allow them to file their affidavit in reply."
The High Court was scheduled today to hear the judicial review application by Altantuya's family seeking to compel police to investigate the supplementary affidavit and statutory declaration by Azilah, who was convicted in the murder of the Mongolian model.
On Oct 16, 2025, High Court judge Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, who is now a Court of Appeal judge, granted Shaariibuu leave to initiate judicial review proceedings after being informed that the Attorney-General did not object to the application.
In the application, Shaariibuu is seeking a declaration that the respondents' failure to inform him of the status of investigations conducted in 2019 by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department regarding Azilah's affidavits was unlawful.
The supplementary affidavit dated Sept 24, 2024, and the statutory declaration dated Oct 17, 2019, were submitted by Azilah to support his death sentence review application at the Federal Court on Oct 10, 2024.
Both documents contained statements by Azilah alleging he had received orders from "top officials" to execute a "covert operation" to "kill and dispose of the deceased."
Shaariibuu requested a mandamus order directing the respondents to complete the investigation within one month from the court order if the investigation remains ongoing.
He also sought a mandamus order requiring all respondents to disclose detailed updates on the status of the investigation within seven days of the court's decision.
Additionally, Shaariibuu stated that if the respondents decide to classify the investigation paper as No Further Action (NFA), the grounds for that decision must be provided.
On Oct 10, 2024, the Federal Court commuted Azilah's death sentence to 40 years' imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane after allowing his review application for Altantuya's murder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign student attacked coursemate after break-up - Cops
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dissatisfaction over a female coursemate ending their relationship is believed to have driven a foreign student to break into her family home in Taman Sri Bintang, Kepong, and attack her and her sibling.
Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said investigations indicated that the suspect was unhappy with the woman after she ended their relationship.
"The motive points to the suspect's dissatisfaction with the victim for ending their relationship," he said when contacted today.
Anuar said the suspect, who was also a friend and coursemate of the female victim, was currently being treated at the psychiatric ward of Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
He stressed, however, that doctors were still assessing the suspect and no conclusion had been reached on whether he had a mental health condition.
"The suspect is still under observation by doctors and there is no decision yet," he said.
The suspect remains under a seven-day remand order from Sept 30 until tomorrow and is currently at HKL.
The incident occurred at about 5am on Sept 30 when police were called to the house and found signs of a fire outside the premises.
The two siblings were found hiding in a ground-floor toilet, while police arrested the suspect in an upstairs room. He was armed with a knife.
The victims and suspect, who suffered stab wounds, were taken to hospital for treatment.
Of the two siblings injured in the attack, one was discharged on Oct 4 while the other remains warded.
The case is being investigated under Sections 326 and 435 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt using a dangerous weapon and mischief by fire, respectively.
